# PR Review Summary — PR #1 `rpc: refuse to send on a stream connection once stream_close() has begun`

The fix itself is sound. I traced every interaction between `_stream_closing`, `_error`, `_outgoing_queue_ready`, `_sink_closed_future`, `stop_send_loop()`, `withdraw()`, `abort()` and `stop()`, and found no correctness bug in the change to `src/rpc/rpc.cc`. Nothing was built or run: the repo has no build directory and building Seastar for one test was out of scope for a read-only review. All findings below are verified against the code at 69da8f5b.

## Critical Issues (0 found)

None.

## Important Issues (3 found)

- **[code-reviewer] Docs claim any throw from a source read releases it, but serializer errors do not.** `include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:386-388`, `include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:340-342`, `doc/rpc-streaming.md:109-112`. In `include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:942-949` the `process_one_buffer` path calls `unmarshall` outside any handler, so an exception there leaves `_source_closed` false and `stream_close()` never runs. Only failures of `stream_receive()` and eof reach `close_source()` (`rpc_impl.hh:963`, `:969`). An application that follows the new contract literally, stopping at the first throw, will leak the connection. Either document that only eof or a stream failure releases the source and deserialization errors must still be drained, or make `process_one_buffer` failures call `close_source()` too.

- **[pr-test-analyzer, code-reviewer] The queue-drain half of the fix has no test.** `src/rpc/rpc.cc:562-570`. In the new test the outgoing queue is empty by construction when `stream_close()` runs: `close_sink()` is the `.finally` of the already-resolved eof `send()` (`rpc_impl.hh:924`) and the hook fires only after `close_entered`. Deleting the `std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, ...)` wait would fail no test. It is coverable with existing helpers: `c.get_stream(sink.get_id())->get()` gives the stream connection, `suspend_for_testing()` (`include/seastar/rpc/rpc.hh:395`, already used at `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:455`) parks the queue, then fire the hook, then let the source reach eof so `close_source()` runs `stream_close()`, and assert `close_entered` stays false until the dummy is released. That also covers the untested "sink closed first, source eof last" ordering, which is the common one in practice.

- **[silent-failure-hunter, pr-test-analyzer] The test never asserts that the frame was refused.** `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2016-2020`. The `catch (const rpc::closed_error&)` swallows the expected outcome, and a *successful* hook call also passes. Detection then relies entirely on `put_after_close`, which needs the batch flush poller to run before line 2030. Use `BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(stream_send_empty_frame().get(), rpc::closed_error)` and keep the `put_after_close` check as the symptom-level assertion.

## Suggestions (7 found)

- **[pr-test-analyzer] The `yield()` loop does not guarantee the flush poller runs.** `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2022-2024`. `yield()` only schedules an empty task (`src/core/reactor.cc:5009-5014`); pollers run when the queue drains or the quota expires. Without the fix the test still fails, but whether it fails on `put_after_close` or on the `~output_stream` assert is timing dependent, and the comment is inaccurate. `check_for_io_immediately()` forces a poll; the loop becomes unnecessary if the refusal is asserted directly.

- **[comment-analyzer] "_outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed" states the wrong cause.** `src/rpc/rpc.cc:566-567`. A failed `send_entry` calls `abort()` and still runs `p->done.set_value()` (`rpc.cc:333-338`), so a failed entry never makes the chain exceptional. The only sources are `stop_send_loop()` withdrawing queued entries and the `_negotiated` abort (`rpc.cc:206-224`). Say "exceptional if the connection was stopped while entries were still queued", matching the existing comment at `rpc.cc:226-227`.

- **[comment-analyzer] "Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on" is not quite right.** `src/rpc/rpc.cc:559-561`. `stop_send_loop()` still does `when_all` on it (`rpc.cc:225`); it just receives the ready placeholder. Also the retained comment at `rpc.cc:563-564` now sits eight lines away from the `_sink_closed_future = p.get_future()` it explains; move it above line 555.

- **[comment-analyzer] Stale `// send data Out...` and `// receive data In...` lines break the new doxygen blocks.** `include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:343` and `:390`. A plain `//` line now sits between the `///` block and the declaration, and the rest of the file uses a plain first line rather than `\brief` (e.g. `:418`). Remove the old lines and drop `\brief` for consistency.

- **[comment-analyzer] "The stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed" is too strong.** `doc/rpc-streaming.md:114`. The connection is also shut down by a read-loop failure or by closing the parent client via `abort_all_streams()` (`src/rpc/rpc.cc:848-855`), which the doc itself says a few paragraphs earlier. Drop "only" or say "orderly shutdown".

- **[pr-test-analyzer] `const_cast` in the hook-capturing factory.** `tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:1957`. Declaring `hooks` as `mutable` is cleaner than casting away const on `this`.

- **[code-reviewer] Attribution trailers violate your global CLAUDE.md rule.** The PR body ends with a "Generated with Claude Code" line and all three commits carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailers. Your instructions say never to add these; strip them before merge.

## Strengths

- **The core race analysis is correct and the fix is minimal.** Exchanging `_outgoing_queue_ready` is safe: `stop_send_loop()` still serializes on `_sink_closed_future`, which resolves only after the drain and `write_buf.close()`, and `withdraw()`'s promise swap keeps the drained chain resolving. No hang on `_negotiated` is possible, because `stream_close()` with `!_error` requires an eof frame that can only arrive after negotiation.
- **Every `send()` caller on a stream was checked and behaves correctly.** The eof marker is sent before `close_sink()`, `send_buffer()` is drained by `_send_queue.stop()` first, and both hook sites (`rpc.cc:696`, `:1103`) route through `send()`. The only direct `write_buf` write is the negotiation frame.
- **Error propagation slightly improves.** A synchronous throw from `write_buf.close()` previously escaped `stream_close()` with `p` unset, leaving a broken `_sink_closed_future` that `stop_send_loop()` would `.get()`. Inside `then_wrapped` it now becomes a failed future and `p` is always set.
- **Test object lifetimes are right.** `st` is declared before `sink`/`source`, the connection is deregistered from the parent before `sink.close()` returns, and `hooks.back()` is deterministic because `make_stream_sink` awaits the parent's negotiation.

## Recommended Action

1. Fix the source-release doc claim (or make deserialization failures close the source).
2. Add a queue-drain test using `suspend_for_testing()` and assert the `closed_error` refusal directly.
3. Apply the comment and doxygen corrections, and strip the attribution trailers.
4. Re-run `rpc_test` in the debug (sanitizer) build on 1 and 2 shards after the changes.
